perspective:
**Christian Mensah’s available information**

- Christian is a police officer. Jonathan is his childhood friend/best friend, and Christian often seeks his advice.
- Christian felt Jonathan had been acting differently and became anxious/suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important. He arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop.
- Christian told Jonathan he felt he was hiding something. He heard Jonathan say he could trust him, then admit he had been hiding something and was in trouble but didn’t know how to tell him.
- Christian offered help and support. He heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated and he didn’t want to drag him in. Christian insisted they face it together; Jonathan said he could use support/resources and needed to get out of the mess.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. He heard Jonathan say he couldn’t say for sure, might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into it discreetly for Jonathan’s safety. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted him to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian concluded that Jonathan was being framed. He told Jonathan this, said he didn’t yet know who was responsible but had leads, and planned to gather evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Later, Christian believed/claimed he had found out who was behind it: someone both he and Jonathan knew and trusted. He felt betrayed and resolute, decided to confront this person, and told Jonathan he would bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person was dangerous but trusted him.
